gaps.description: Claims a full quit-and-restart of Claude Code is required before a newly added skill becomes usable. In Claude Code, running /reload-plugins picks up new skills without restarting; on other platforms, new skills are available immediately on next session start.
gaps.corpus_ref: MISCONCEPTION: you have to restart Claude to use new skills

gaps.description: States as fact that there is 'no lighter-weight way to refresh the skill list,' which is factually wrong — /reload-plugins is exactly that lighter-weight mechanism.
gaps.corpus_ref: MISCONCEPTION: you have to restart Claude to use new skills

gaps.description: Does not mention /reload-plugins, does not distinguish Claude Code's refresh behavior from other platforms' next-session-start behavior, and omits install-skills-flat.sh's role.
Gives no account of how skill discovery/loading actually works across the different supported platforms, each of which has its own refresh behavior.
gaps.corpus_ref: MISCONCEPTION: skills only work on Claude Code

transfer_problems: You just ran install-skills-flat.sh to add a brand-new skill directory under skills/react/. A teammate is using Claude Code and wants to use it right away without restarting their session — what command should they run, and why does that work without a full restart?

A teammate on OpenCode adds a new skill folder mid-session and expects it to appear immediately the way /reload-plugins works in Claude Code, but it does not show up. Explain what they should actually expect and do to pick up the new skill.
